Use BuildChooserContext environment in InverseBuildChooser

Fixes an issue.

When polling git for changes, context.getBuild() returns null, manifesting in an NPE from  InverseBuildChooser.getCandidateRevisions() when polling a git repo and using an Inverse branch choosing strategy.

This was fixed for DefaultBuildChooser in 68331baf78649becac426b9362534faff08cf618--BuildChooserContext now includes the appropriate environment, so there is no longer any need to call context.getBuild().getEnvironment() as demonstrated in [DefaultBuildChooser.java](https://github.com/jenkinsci/git-plugin/commit/68331baf78649becac426b9362534faff08cf618#diff-59b21aee0282fdafd62036844373a19cL190).

Fix org.getMembers() to 'wrap' returned users for post-populating

This fixes an issue in which users returned by `getMembers()` were not
populated with a full set of values.

This commit just applies 'wrapping' to all users returned, so that methods
like `user.getCreatedAt()` can be called on returned users without throwing
a NullPointerException - the reference to 'root' allows the user objects to
populate themselves.

Speed up deletes and updates of the 'words' table

FTS3 virtual tables don't support user-defined indices -- not even a
primary key. So let's use the rowid instead, which will significantly
speed up the delete/update-cascading triggers.

Also, fix two bugs. The row's
ID was intended to be equal to the corresponding sms._id, or the
corresponding part._id+(2<<32) for mms. However:

* In Java, the second operator for int shifts is modulo 32, so
  (2<<32) == (2<<0) == 2. Making the shifted value a long fixes it.
* The populateWordsTable method (which ran on upgrade) didn't add the
  offset at all.

With this fixed, we can get rid of the unindexable source_id and
table_to_use columns, which I can only assume were added because the
id offsetting scheme was not working as intended. We have no use for
the _id column either. We can drop and recreate the table easily, since
all the data is present in other tables anyway.

MINOR: fix a bug in removing elements from an ImplicitLinkedHashColle…

Fix a bug that resulted in incorrect behavior when
deleting through an iterator.

The bug is that the hash table relies on a denseness invariant... if you remove something,
you might have to move some other things. Calling removeElementAtSlot will do this.
Calling removeFromList is not enough.
